title: Character, Calling & Conviction
audience: Pastors and missionaries · opening overview, first of four speakers
bigIdea: His power isn't about how we change ourselves. It's about what He makes us into.

verses.text: Apart from me you can do NOTHING.

**__No branch can bear fruit by itself__**; it must remain in the vine...   “I am the vine; you are the branches. If you remain in me and I in you, you will bear much fruit; **apart from me you can do nothing**.

points.script:
[#1 Nothing conference]
[#2 Already ready!]
[#2 I'll ignore Art’s new topic]/
When Art told me what the topic of this conference was originally—NOTHING—I jumped at the chance to speak. That's easy... I can talk about nothing... I already have my talk prepared... Then he changed the topic... So I decided for this conference I would just ignore Art’s new topic and just go with the old “Nothing” topic.
[#1 Walk off stage] 
Today, I am here to talk about [Slow][Exclaim]NOTHING[Normal]. Thank you. [ Walk off the stage - 20 seconds then come back up][Long pause]
[#1 Describe CCS talk]
Just kidding – I actually did that when I spoke at CCS graduation, and when I walked off stage I looked at the MC, who was in terror. What was she going to do? I could see it in her eyes as I walked by her, then she started to go up to the stage to try to continue... I asked her later what she was going to say, and she said, "I don't know – probably 'thank you, Sir Norman, for that wonderful talk about nothing.'" As I thought about it, though, I actually think the concept of Nothing and a talk about Character, Calling and Conviction really do have a lot in common. Let me explain.
[#1 But... Nothing and Character, Calling and Conviction are connected{John 15:1}]
All of us would have used one verse if we were doing a talk about nothing.
[John 15:1]   Apart from me you can do nothing. But what does that mean?

I think that when Jesus said “nothing,” he really meant nothing. Without Jesus, it is impossible for us to do anything. I don't think that those words of Jesus mean that we can’t do a lot, or that what we do will mean more if we do it with Him. I think what Jesus was saying was that whatever we do apart from Him IS nothing; it has no eternal value. [Exclaim]NONE[Normal].
Now, it is important to understand what the context of this phrase was. What was He talking about when He said this?

points.slide:
They are fruit...

...and we cannot produce fruit by ourselves.
points.script:
[#1 Vines, branches and fruit]
[#2 Are CCC fruit?] He was talking about fruit. A vine and branches and fruit. Bearing fruit... abiding in Him... and if we abide... much fruit. I think we can agree from this verse that if we are not abiding in Him, we cannot produce fruit. None.

So, here is a question for you. Are Character, Calling and Conviction fruit? If you try hard enough by yourself, without Jesus, can you have good character? Can you strive to have a strong conviction? Can you be called to ANYTHING?
I think the best example I have of this is the disciples.
[#1 Disciples]
 Let me ask a question. How did the disciples get their character, their calling and their conviction?

Did they get it when they walked with Jesus for three years? They heard every sermon. They saw every miracle. They had the best discipleship program in history, and the teacher was Jesus Himself. While He was here on earth they worked to understand. They tried to follow.

So, when Jesus was done teaching them, did they have it?  What was the result of those three years? We don't have to guess.

verses.text: Then everyone deserted him and fled.

The Lord turned and looked straight at Peter. Then Peter remembered the word the Lord had spoken to him: "Before the rooster crows today, you will disown me three times." And he went outside and wept bitterly.
On the evening of that first day of the week, when the disciples were together, with the doors locked for fear of the Jewish leaders, Jesus came and stood among them and said, "Peace be with you!"

points.script:
[#1 All of the time with Jesus seemed to mean nothing]
[#2 In Mark, they all fled]
[#2 In Luke, denied 3 times]
[#2 In John huddled and afraid]After Jesus was gone they were huddled together in a locked room, afraid and shaking. They were destroyed. Jesus was dead. Their dreams were gone. Their conviction was lost. Their character? Quitters! Their calling? A lost dream. The one they believed in was dead. Now what? They said "Lets hiding and hopefully they don’t find us and kill us."

After all the time with Jesus. After all the miracles. After all His teaching. After the countless discussions over dinner. After all the personal one-on-one time. [Slow]ALL OF THEM[Normal] left. ALL of them left their conviction in the dust. They were failures and losers. Now what? All of their plans, their calling to change the world... all gone.

It is obvious that even after being with Jesus… even after all their effort and trying… NONE of them developed true character, NONE of them developed conviction to die for what they believed, NONE of them knew what it really meant to be called.

In Mark, they all deserted Him and fled.
In Luke, Peter denied Jesus three times.
In John, after the cross, where do we find them? Behind locked doors and afraid. The men who would one day turn the world upside down were hiding in a room. No real convictions, no real character and no real calling.
[#1 And that would have been the end...]
And that would have been the end. [Pause] As Jesus had already predicted it… their character, their calling and their conviction were NOTHING without Him. In fact, they wern't theirs at all.

verses.text: Then they gathered around him and asked him, “Lord, are you at this time going to restore the kingdom to Israel?

points.script:
Then Jesus was back, he spent more time with them.   When he was leaving... [#1 Acts 1:6] Acts 1:6 – Then they gathered around him and asked him, “Lord, are you at this time going to restore the kingdom to Israel?”
[#1 No lesson learned]
Can you picture the scene as the disciples, excited to see Jesus back from the dead, ask this question in Acts 1:6: "Lord, are you at this time going to restore the kingdom to Israel?"

I am sure they thought, "Finally… now we can get going again. Jesus is back and nothing is going to stop us now!"

They still didn't get it. Is now the time? You're going to restore your kingdom and it is easy for us! They were looking for the easy way out. Now I really don't need conviction or character or calling. You set up your kingdom and we are in charge now. The hard part is over.

But no, the hard part wasn't over—but something WAS going to change.

verses.text: But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you; and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.

points.script:
[#1 ...And then {Acts 1:8}][Acts 1:8]Acts 1:8 - But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you; 

That next phrase brought even more excitement. I am sure they thought, "Awesome! We get power!" but little did they know what lay ahead. Although it was full of power, it was also full of trials, hard times, persecutions and even death.

If I want to experience the power of God in my life, I should expect nothing different. It is His power, but in the midst of difficulties, hard times and struggles.
"You shall receive power" will bring opposition.
"You shall receive power" will bring difficulties.
"You shall receive power" will bring hard times.  it will bring Jail
"You shall receive power" will bring conflict.  it will bring thorns in the flesh
"You shall receive power" WILL reveal our weakness.

But then...

In our weakness He is strong.
In our weakness He works in mighty ways.
In our weakness He brings healing.
In our weakness He saves people.  He brings revival, he transforms us.
In our weakness He changes the world.

Don't expect that "you shall receive power" will look any different in your life than it did for the disciples.

points.slideTitle:
The disciples received power
and it brought prison, conflict and weakness.
points.slide: Don't expect it to look any different.

verses.text: They called the apostles in and had them flogged. Then they ordered them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and let them go. The apostles left the Sanhedrin, rejoicing because they had been counted worthy of suffering disgrace for the Name.

But the Lord said to Ananias, "Go! This man is my chosen instrument to proclaim my name to the Gentiles and their kings and to the people of Israel. I will show him how much he must suffer for my name."

points.script:
[#1 Acts 4: Peter and John in jail]
[#2 Stephen stoned, James killed, church scattered]
[#2 Paul: called and told how much he'd suffer (Acts 9:16)] And look at what happened next. Within a few chapters, Peter and John are in jail. Then all the apostles are arrested, flogged, and ordered never to speak in the name of Jesus again. 
[#1 ddfdf]
Stephen is stoned. James is killed with the sword. The church is scattered. They expected a throne; they got a difficult road.

When Jesus calls Paul, He tells Ananias, "This man is my chosen instrument," and in the same breath, "I will show him how much he must suffer for my name." The calling and the suffering came in the same sentence.

The word Jesus used for witness is martys, the word we get martyr from. When He said, "You will be my witnesses," they had no idea yet what that word would come to mean.

The disciples received power, and it brought prison, conflict, and weakness.

So don't expect it to look any different for you. I think a lot of us in ministry carry a quiet expectation: If I'm really called, if God's power is really on me, things should go well. The church should grow. The money should come in. The board should agree with me. And when it doesn't, we wonder what we did wrong.

Maybe we didn't do anything wrong. Maybe that's just what the power looks like.

[#1 Expected a throne, got a road]


[#1 Our quiet expectation: "if I'm called, it should go well"]
[#1 Maybe that's what the power looks like]

points.slide:
The disciples didn't produce them. 

His power produced them.

verses.text: When they saw the courage of Peter and John and realized that they were unschooled, ordinary men, they were astonished and they took note that these men had been with Jesus.

points.script:
[#1 Same Peter: servant girl → Sanhedrin]
But look at what happened to these men. The same Peter who couldn't stand up to a servant girl by a fire now stands up before the Sanhedrin, the most powerful men in Jerusalem.

[#1 "Unschooled, ordinary men... had been with Jesus"]
And the leaders looked at Peter and John, saw that they were unschooled, ordinary men, and they were astonished. And they took note that these men had been with Jesus.

Where did that courage come from? Where did that character come from? Not from a seminar. [#1 Not a seminar, not trying harder] Not from trying harder.

[#1 🔁 Character, calling, conviction. They didn't make them. His power produced them.]
Character, calling, conviction. They didn't make themselves. His power produced them.

sections.title: What the power makes us into

points.slideTitle: His power isn't about how we change ourselves.
points.slide: It's about what He makes us into.

verses.text: But the pot he was shaping from the clay was marred in his hands; so the potter formed it into another pot, shaping it as seemed best to him.

points.script:
[#1 We argue about what the power looks like]
Now, we can argue a lot about what that power is supposed to look like and what it is supposed to do. Some of us say the power is about miracles and healing and signs. [#1 Miracles vs. "God doesn't work that way now"] Some of us say God doesn't really work that way anymore. [#1 Not arguing today] And we could spend this whole conference arguing about it.

I don't want to argue today. [#1 Wrong question: what it does] I want to suggest that maybe we're asking the wrong question. We keep asking what the power does. [#1 Jesus: what it makes them into ("you will BE")] Jesus was describing what the power would make them into. He didn't say, "You will do witnessing." He said, "You will be my witnesses."

Jeremiah went down to the potter's house and watched him work. [#1 Potter: marred pot, formed into another] The pot was marred in his hands, so the potter didn't throw the clay away. He formed it into another pot, shaping it as seemed best to him.

[#1 🔑 "His power isn't about how we change ourselves. It's about what He makes us into."]
His power isn't about how we change ourselves. It's about what He makes us into.

verses.text: But he said to me, "My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness." Therefore I will boast all the more gladly about my weaknesses, so that Christ's power may rest on me. That is why, for Christ's sake, I delight in weaknesses, in insults, in hardships, in persecutions, in difficulties. For when I am weak, then I am strong.

points.script:
[#1 Acts 1:8 power = dynamis]
The word Jesus uses for power in Acts 1:8 is *dynamis*. [#1 Same word: 2 Cor 12:9] And it is the same word Paul uses in 2 Corinthians 12:9, when the Lord tells him, "My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness."

Same word. Same power.

[#1 We love "dynamite"]
We get our word "dynamite" from it, and we love that. We want the dynamite. But look where Paul found it. [#1 Paul begged 3x for the thorn to go] [#1 God said no: power made perfect in weakness] He had begged God three times to take his thorn away, and God said no. So Paul says, "I will boast all the more gladly about my weaknesses, so that Christ's power may rest on me... [#1 "When I am weak, then I am strong"] For when I am weak, then I am strong."

verses.text: Peter declared, "Even if all fall away, I will not." "Truly I tell you," Jesus answered, "today, yes, tonight, before the rooster crows twice you yourself will disown me three times." But Peter insisted emphatically, "Even if I have to die with you, I will never disown you." And all the others said the same.
When they had finished eating, Jesus said to Simon Peter, "Simon son of John, do you love me more than these?" "Yes, Lord," he said, "you know that I love you." Jesus said, "Feed my lambs."

points.script:
[#1 Peter the strong one: first to speak, out of the boat, the sword]
Go back to Peter. Peter was the strong one. He was the first to speak, the first to step out of the boat, the first to pull out a sword in the garden. He cut off a man's ear. [#1 The ear: strength without character] That was strength without character.

[#1 "Even if all fall away, I never will"]
Peter was the one who said, "Even if all fall away, I will not." [#1 Real conviction, but his own] That was his conviction, and he meant it. But it was his conviction, not God's. [#1 Failed by a fire, a servant girl] And it failed him by a fire, in front of a servant girl.

I learned this one as a dad. I could be a pretty legalistic father. I was focused on my kids' behavior, not what was going on in their hearts. [#1 Me as a dad: my conviction in them washed away] And as they grew up, a lot of those behaviors just washed away, because it was my conviction in them. It was never their own. Conviction that is put on you from the outside doesn't hold. [#1 Conviction must be planted inside] It has to be planted on the inside.

[#1 The look, wept bitterly]
Luke tells us that the Lord turned and looked straight at Peter, and Peter went outside and wept bitterly. That night by the fire, something in Peter broke. And it had to.

Then, a few weeks later, there's another fire. [#1 Second fire: breakfast on the beach] Jesus makes breakfast on the beach. [#1 Three denials, three questions: "Feed my sheep"] Three denials, and now three questions: "Peter, do you love me?" "Feed my sheep." The calling comes back, but this time it isn't resting on Peter's strength.

[#1 Had to break his self-sufficiency]
Before God could use Peter, he had to break Peter's self-sufficiency. I believe God cannot use someone who is not broken.

points.slide: We spend our whole lives striving to be strong, when God is calling us to be weak.
points.script:
[#1 Hard part for leaders]
And this is the hard part for us as leaders. [#1 We got here by being strong] Most of us got where we are because we were strong. We were the ones who could handle it. People look to us. [#1 Have the answer, fix the problem] We have to have the answer, preach the sermon, fix the problem, keep the ministry going. Nobody hires a weak pastor. [#1 "Nobody sends a weak missionary"] Nobody sends out a weak missionary.

I know this one personally. [#1 Me: 30 years in business, the one they called when things broke] I spent about thirty years in business, and I was the one they called when things broke. Being strong was my job.

[#1 Watchman Nee: "Effort is not the key to maturity; death is."]
Watchman Nee said, "Effort is not the key to maturity; death is." That is not the kind of thing you put on a leadership poster.

[#1 🔑 "We spend our whole lives striving to be strong, when God is calling us to be weak."]
We spend our whole lives striving to be strong, when God is calling us to be weak.

verses.text: I planted the seed, Apollos watered it, but God has been making it grow. So neither the one who plants nor the one who waters is anything, but only God, who makes things grow.

points.script:
[#1 Dad, Gene: ~30 yrs Navigators in PH]
My dad, Gene Denler, was a missionary here in the Philippines for about thirty years with the Navigators. [#1 Effort focused: "It's you, it's you"] He was very effort‑focused. It was always, "It's you, it's you."

[#1 Left the field broken]
He left the field feeling broken. [#1 Construction supervisor for my uncle] He wondered what his life had really accomplished, and he ended up working as a construction supervisor for my uncle. [#1 Changed with age: never about his effort] As he got older, he came to see that it was never about his effort. By the time he died, he was a different person.

In 2009, when he was 81, my dad came back to the Philippines with my family. [#1 2009: hospital at St. Luke's, saw his old disciples still serving] He ended up in the hospital with blood clots in both legs, at St. Luke's, the same hospital where I was born. And because of that interruption, he got to sit with some of the men he had discipled as teenagers forty years earlier, still serving God in their sixties. [#1 "We sow, we water... God makes it grow"] He wrote, "It humbled me to realize anew that we sow, we water, but it's God that makes it grow."

[#1 His "faulty ministry model" → "He is enough!"]
On that same trip, he wrote about what he called "a faulty ministry model" that had been part of his DNA—the idea that you have to aggressively make it happen through strategies and programs. And he wrote about being drawn instead to the way Jesus simply went about doing good. He ended it with three words: "He is enough!"

But even then, he didn't see all of it. [#1 Discipled two young men when I was three] When I was three years old, my mom and dad were discipling two young men in our home. [#1 Today: our school director and our pastor, ~20 yrs] One of them is the director of our school today. The other is the pastor of the church. They have been foundational to this ministry for about twenty years.

[#1 Thought it came to nothing. God wasn't done.]
My dad thought it came to nothing. God wasn't done.

[#1 Slide up, silence]
So let me ask you.

Are you broken?

(Pause. Let it sit.)

[#1 Maybe you came here broken]
Maybe you came to this conference broken. [#1 Church, marriage, money, your own heart] Maybe it’s your church, your marriage, your finances, or your own heart. [#1 Feels like your work came to nothing] [#1 Not the end, maybe the beginning] Maybe, like my dad, you feel like your work has come to nothing.

[#1 "In the ministry of love, only the wounded can serve."]
My dad quoted someone who said, "In the ministry of love, only the wounded can serve."

[#1 🔑 "God cannot use someone who is not broken. If you are, you're exactly where He wants you to be."]
God cannot use someone who is not broken. If you are, you're exactly where He wants you to be.

That isn’t the end of your ministry. It may be the beginning of it.

points.slide: We don't make them. His power makes them in our weakness.

verses.text: But we have this treasure in jars of clay to show that this all-surpassing power is from God and not from us.

points.script:
[#1 Kintsugi: broken bowl repaired with gold]
[#1 Worth more than before it broke]
In Japan there's an art called kintsugi. When a bowl breaks, they don't throw it away. They put it back together with gold. And the bowl becomes more valuable than it was before it broke. [#1 The cracks are where the gold is] The cracks are where the gold is.

[#1 Treasure in jars of clay]
Paul says, "We have this treasure in jars of clay to show that this all-surpassing power is from God and not from us."

[#1 🔁 Character, calling, conviction. We don't make them. His power makes them in our weakness.]
Character, calling, conviction. We don't make them. His power makes them in our weakness.

verses.text: Many are the plans in a person's heart, but it is the LORD's purpose that prevails.

points.script:
[#1 2017: came to KIDS, ministry hurting]
Let me tell you where I learned this. When I came to KIDS in 2017, the ministry was hurting. [#1 Damaged by past leadership] It had been damaged by past leadership. [#1 Money a struggle every month] [#1 Prayer: "Leadership, leadership, leadership"] Every month was a struggle for money, and I prayed one prayer over and over: "Leadership, leadership, leadership."

[#1 Left business: lives impacted, not revenue]
I had left business because I was tired of measuring my life by how much revenue I created for a company. I wanted to measure my life by the lives I impacted. But I brought my business habits with me. [#1 Came in like a CTO: plans, budgets, systems] I came in like a CTO—plans, budgets, fundraising, systems.

And it took me a long time to get here. I felt called to missions when I was young. [#1 My calling, delayed: Dad objected, went into business] My dad was actually the one who objected the most. I think he had been burnt by ministry, and he wanted his son to have a job and a foundation. So I went into business. For years I wondered why I didn't go sooner. [#1 Years of preparation; calling = who He makes you] Now I can see that those years were preparation. God wasn't wasting them. He had things to do in me first. Calling isn't just a job you get. It's someone He makes you into.

And I worked. I believed it was up to me to fix it. [#1 "Christ in me," but lived like it was up to me] I would have told you it was Christ in me, but I lived like it was all up to me.

[#1 2019: healthier, still no leaders, tired]
By 2019 the ministry was somewhat healthy. The finances were better. But the leaders I had prayed for still weren't there. And I was tired.

[#1 2020: everything stopped]
Then 2020 came, and everything stopped. We were shut in. [#1 Shut in, two weeks of nothing] For two weeks, we did nothing. [#1 No money coming in, no plan] There was no money coming in, and I had no plan.

Everything I knew how to do didn’t work. [#1 Couldn't fundraise or plan my way out] I couldn’t fundraise my way out of it. I couldn’t plan my way out of it. Everything I had been leaning on—my experience, my strength, my systems—was gone.

[#1 For the first time in a long time: nothing]
For the first time in a long time, I had nothing.

[#1 Hungry families at our gate]
Then hungry families started coming to us, asking for food. [#1 Cooking at the market] So we started cooking and handing out meals at the market. [#1 Local government asked for food] [#1 "Can we also feed the pastors?"] Then the local government came and asked us for food, and I said, "Can we also feed the pastors?"

One of our pastors, Pastora Grace, said it this way: "We are not afraid of COVID-19. We are more afraid of people dying because of hunger."

[#1 3,000 → 250,000 meals a week]
[#1 Pastora Grace: more afraid of hunger than COVID]
We went from about 3,000 meals a week to about 250,000 meals a week. [#1 Didn't plan it; couldn't afford it] I didn't plan that. Nobody would plan that. We didn't have the money for 3,000 meals, much less 250,000.

[#1 Birthed youth + family ministry, clinic ×10, 1,000+ pastors]
And out of that season came things we never could have built: a youth ministry, a family ministry. Our clinic grew about ten times. More than a thousand pastors connected with us through those feedings.

[#1 At the table: time to stop the feeding]
One day we were sitting around a table, talking about stopping the feeding. There was no money. [#1 Pastor Art: "We can't. There's people who are hungry, Norman."] Pastor Art looked at me and said, "We can't. There are people who are hungry, Norman."

[#1 "There's no money," walked away]
I told him there was no money, and I got up and walked away from the table. [#1 Phone: former boss, not a Christian] I looked at my phone, and there was a message from my former boss. He is not a Christian. [#1 His board: $50,000] He said his board wanted to donate $50,000.

[#1 "Never mind. The money came in."]
I walked back to the table and said, "Never mind. The money came in."

I didn't raise that money. [#1 Not my strength; God was already there] I walked away from that table with nothing, and God was already there. And we have so many stories from that season just like that one.

points.slideTitle: When I strive in my strength, I burn out.
points.slide: When I strive in His, I'm refreshed.

verses.text: To this end I strenuously contend with all the energy Christ so powerfully works in me.

points.script:
[#1 The leaders came, the ones I prayed for]
And then the leaders came, the ones I had been praying for—people we had never been connected to before. [#1 Pastor Art: partner in the feedings] Pastor Art became my partner in the feedings. [#1 His son: Youth Lab, first youth ministry] His son started Youth Lab, the first youth ministry we ever had. [#1 Volunteers quarantined together → missionaries] Volunteers who quarantined together at the ministry center caught a passion and became missionaries. [#1 0 → 26 Filipino missionaries] We went from zero Filipino missionaries to twenty-six. And they brought a whole new culture with them, a passion for prayer that we hadn't had before.

[#1 Hardest and most beautiful season]
It was the hardest time of my life, and the most beautiful. [#1 Up at 4am, working till 10 or 11pm, loved it] I was up at four in the morning and working until ten or eleven at night, and I enjoyed every moment of it.

I used to windsurf. [#1 Windsurfing: I don't make the wind] When you windsurf, you don't make the wind. You can't. You can pull on that sail as hard as you want, and if there's no wind, you go nowhere. But when the wind comes and you catch it, you fly. You're still working. Every muscle is working. But it doesn't drain you. It's the most fun you'll ever have.

[#1 Col 1:29: all His energy]
That's what Paul means in Colossians 1:29: "To this end I strenuously contend with all the energy Christ so powerfully works in me." Paul is working hard, but the energy is Christ's.

[#1 🔑 "When I strive in my strength, I burn out. When I strive in His, I'm refreshed."]
When I strive in my strength, I burn out. When I strive in His, I'm refreshed.

points.slide: If I can do it myself, it isn't faith.

verses.text: Now faith is confidence in what we hope for and assurance about what we do not see.

points.script:
[#1 Building a high school, poor community]
[#1 Still not finished: more floors, an auditorium]
We are building a high school on land in a poor community, and it is still not finished. There are classrooms full of kids, and there are still more storeys and an auditorium to go. People ask me how we are going to finish it. [#1 "How will you finish it?" I don't know] I don't know. [#1 If I can see it on a spreadsheet, I need a calculator, not faith] [#1 "If God's love is extravagant, why not the school?"] When we first walked that land, I asked myself, if God's love is extravagant, why shouldn't the school be?

Hebrews says faith is confidence in what we hope for and assurance about what we do not see. If I can already see how it gets done—if the money is in the bank and the plan is on the spreadsheet—I don't need faith. I need a calculator.

[#1 🔑 "If I can do it myself, it isn't faith."]
I have learned this: if I can do it myself, it isn't faith.

[#1 (Optional, judgment call on the day)]
[#1 A very personal season]
[#1 My conviction about my life gave way]
[#1 Not going into it]
(Optional, judgment call on the day.) There was also a season in my own life, a very personal one, when my own conviction about how my life would go simply gave way. [#1 God used the loss to change me] I won't go into it today, but God used that loss to change me in ways my strength never could.

verses.text: Not only so, but we also glory in our sufferings, because we know that suffering produces perseverance; perseverance, character; and character, hope.

points.script:
[#1 I'm not the strong one; I never was]
So that's what I learned. I'm not the strong one; I never was. [#1 Same pattern as Peter, as my dad] It's the same pattern we saw in Peter, and in my dad. God let the strength run out so He could be the strength.

Paul says suffering produces perseverance, and perseverance produces character. Character isn't something you build on a good day.

[#1 🔁 Character, calling, conviction. We don't make them. His power forms them in our weakness.]
Character, calling, conviction. We don't make them. His power makes them in our weakness.

points.slide: Ministry is messy, and there's beauty in the mess.
points.script:
[#1 CCC sound tidy: in a box, checked off]
Character, calling, and conviction sound very tidy, don't they? Like something you could put in a box and check off. Character, check. Calling, check. Conviction, check.

[#1 The opposite is true]
The opposite is true.

[#1 Painter's palette: a mess]
Look at a painter's palette. It's a mess. Colors smeared everywhere, blobs, drips, brushes dipped in three colors at once. If all you ever saw was the palette, you'd say, what a mess. But somewhere behind it, there's a painting. [#1 Every painting started on a messy palette] Every beautiful painting started on a messy palette.

Ministry is messy, and there's beauty in the mess. [#1 If life were straight lines, we wouldn't need God] If life were all straight lines, we wouldn't need God. [#1 God puts us where the mess shows up] [#1 🔑 "Ministry is messy, and there's beauty in the mess."] And I've come to believe God intentionally puts us right where the mess shows up, so that He can be the one who makes it work.

[#1 Mess teaches humility]
The mess teaches us humility. [#1 I'm not in control; I can't fix it] I'm not in control, and I can't fix it.

[#1 Expect clean → disappointed → angry]
And if I expect it to be clean, I will be disappointed, and then I will be angry—angry at my staff, angry at the board, angry at the pastors who didn't show up, and, if I'm honest, angry at God.

[#1 Dad: the small interruptions are harder than the big trials]
My dad once said it's easier not to question God about the big trials than about the small daily interruptions. The big things we give to God. It's the little things that get under our skin.

[#1 Even now, strained relationships; God at work in the middle]
Even right now, there are relationships in our ministry that are strained. It's messy. And I am seeing God at work everywhere in the middle of it.

[#1 Expect the mess, and God in it]
So expect the mess. And expect God in it.

points.slide: I find God's voice in the doing, not just the waiting.

verses.text: In his defense Jesus said to them, "My Father is always at his work to this very day, and I too am working." ... Jesus gave them this answer: "Very truly I tell you, the Son can do nothing by himself; he can do only what he sees his Father doing, because whatever the Father does the Son also does."

points.script:
[#1 Blackaby: find where God is working, join Him]
Henry Blackaby taught us to find where God is working and join Him. [#1 Jesus: "My Father is always at work"] Jesus said, "My Father is always at his work to this very day, and I too am working." And, "The Son can do nothing by himself; he can do only what he sees his Father doing."

[#1 Not my best place: sitting still for hours]
I'll be honest: sitting still for hours is not where I hear God best. I've tried. For me, I find God's voice in the doing, not just the waiting.

[#1 Try something, see if God blesses it]
[#1 Adjust, or move on]
I try something, I see if God blesses it, and I adjust or I move on. A hungry family at the gate. A pastor who needs food. [#1 Hungry family, a pastor, a volunteer who won't go home] A volunteer who doesn't want to go home. That's where the Father is working, and I join Him. COVID taught me that. Where God goes, go there. Don't expect God to follow us. Sometimes a disaster is the biggest opportunity He gives you.

[#1 Whole life becomes my prayer life]
[#1 "Where God goes, go there. Don't expect God to follow us."]
[#1 🔑 "I find God's voice in the doing, not just the waiting."]
My whole life becomes my prayer life.

verses.text: The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth.

points.script:
[#1 Balance: don't go looking for mess]
[#1 Don't create it]
Now, that doesn't mean we go looking for mess, or that we create it. Some of us are very good at creating it. [#1 Bring God's order into it] We bring God's order into it.

That's what Christ did. [#1 Christ didn't stand outside our mess] He didn't stand outside our mess and tell us to clean it up. He came down into the middle of it. [#1 "The Word became flesh"] "The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us."

[#1 Born in a feeding trough, in a barn]
He was born in a barn and laid in a feeding trough with the animals. That is about as messy as it gets. [#1 God's answer to the mess: a baby in a manger] God's answer to our mess wasn't a memo. It was a baby in a manger.

[#1 Tondo 2009: Grace, Lola Maming's mangoes]
In 2009, my wife Tina and I were in Tondo, and we handed a bag of groceries to a woman named Grace. She worked the streets. She came to the Bible study under the bridge, and on the second day, she wept, overwhelmed by how much Jesus loved her. Then an old woman who sold mangoes, Lola Maming, brought us a kilo of mangoes she couldn't afford to give. We took them so she could give. And then we found out Lola Maming was Grace's aunt. [#1 "Probably the only Jesus many had ever seen"] My dad wrote, "We were probably the only Jesus many of them had ever seen." That's what it looks like to bring His order into the mess. You go in.

points.slideTitle: God doesn't see a point in time.

verses.text: being confident of this, that he who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion until the day of Christ Jesus.

points.script:
[#1 In the middle of the mess, remember:]
And when you are in the middle of the mess, remember this.

[#1 Dad's circus story: knothole vs. up in the tree]
My dad used to tell a story about two boys at the circus. One watched through a knothole in the fence, and he saw one animal at a time going by. The other boy was up in a tree, and he saw the whole circus at one glance. [#1 "God sees at one glance every episode of our lives"] My dad said, "God sees at one glance every episode of our lives."

[#1 Don't judge your ministry, or anyone else, by one frame]
So don't judge your ministry by one frame. And don't judge anyone else's by one frame either. [#1 He who began a good work will finish it] He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion.

[#1 🔑 "God doesn't see a point in time. He sees the whole journey."]
God doesn't see a point in time. He sees the whole journey.

points.slide: We don't make them. His power makes them in the mess.

verses.text: for it is God who works in you to will and to act in order to fulfill his good purpose.

points.script:
[#1 Paul's best letters: from prison]
Remember, Paul wrote some of his most beautiful letters from prison. [#1 Philippians: joy, from a cell] Philippians, a letter about joy, was written in chains. The mess didn't stop what God was doing in him. The mess was where God was doing it. [#1 "It is God who works in you" (Phil 2:13)] And in that same letter, he writes, "It is God who works in you to will and to act in order to fulfill his good purpose"—from a prison cell.

[#1 🔁 Character, calling, conviction. We don't make them. His power makes them in the mess.]
Character, calling, conviction. We don't make them. His power makes them in the mess.

[#1 Callback: "Don't expect it to look any different"]
At the beginning, I told you not to expect His power to look any different for you than it did for the disciples. [#1 Don't expect the mess to be different either] Don't expect the mess to be any different either.

[#1 The power and the mess: the same thing]
The power and the mess aren't two different things. They're the same thing.

If you go home from this conference and things get hard, don't think the power left you. That may be the very moment it's working. Peter by the fire. My dad in that hospital bed. Me at that table with no money. The mess is not a sign that God left.

points.slide: The mess is where the power lives.

verses.text: For the message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God. ... For the foolishness of God is wiser than human wisdom, and the weakness of God is stronger than human strength.

points.script:
Because the mess is where the power lives.

[#1 Started in a manger, ended at a cross]
It started in a manger and went all the way to a cross. Think about the cross. [#1 Cross: biggest mess in history] From the outside, it was the biggest mess in all of history: the Son of God, beaten, mocked, hanging between two criminals, His friends gone. [#1 And the greatest display of His power] And it was the greatest display of God's power the world has ever seen.

[#1 Foolishness to some; to us, the power of God]
[#1 🔑 "The mess is where the power lives."]
Paul says, "The message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God." The weakness of God is stronger than human strength.

points.slideTitle: There's a thin line between faith and insanity.
points.script:
[#1 High school: people thought I was crazy]
When we started building the high school, people thought I was crazy. [#1 Sometimes I did too] Some days, I thought I was crazy too.

[#1 From outside, faith and insanity look the same]
From the outside, faith and insanity can look exactly the same. [#1 Never near the line → never need faith] And if you never go anywhere near that line, you will never need faith. Walking the line doesn't mean doing something foolish; it means doing the next thing He shows you, even when you can't see how it ends.

[#1 🔑 "There's a thin line between faith and insanity. Walk the line."]
There's a thin line between faith and insanity. Walk the line.

verses.text: For we are God's handiwork, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance for us to do.

points.script:
[#1 Came to talk about nothing after all]
It turns out I came to talk about nothing after all.

[#1 Remember the branch]
Remember the branch. [#1 Apart from Him, nothing. In Him, fruit.] Apart from Him, nothing. In Him, fruit.

[#1 Not bad news: it was never up to you]
And that isn't bad news. It's the best news I know. It means it was never up to you. We are His handiwork, created in Christ Jesus for good works He prepared in advance. He's the one doing the making.

So, as you go into the next three sessions—as we go deep on character, and on calling, and on conviction—I want you to remember where they come from.

points.slide: Listen for what He's making you into.
points.script:
[#1 Read the closing paragraph]
[#1 Kingdom → power → made them different]
The disciples asked for a kingdom, and Jesus gave them power. But it didn't make life easier; it made them different. [#1 Peter's conviction failed by a fire] Peter had his own conviction: "I will never deny you." And it failed him by a fire, in front of a servant girl. [#1 God formed, clarified, planted: His] Then, through prison, persecution, and failure, God did what Peter never could: He formed a character that was His, made clear a calling that was His, and planted a conviction that was His. It still works that way. [#1 "Don't listen for what you need to do for God"] [#1 "Listen for what He's making you into"] [#1 Hand off to the next three speakers] So over the next three sessions, don't listen for what you need to do for God. Listen for what He's making you into.
